correctness.rationale: For strict face chains the size sequence distinguishes all vertices and subfaces within each closed simplex, so the quotient has regular flag-orbit cells with alternating deletion boundaries. An independent representative enumeration using prefix stabilizers rebuilt the eight symmetries and counts (16,78,140,79) and (50,283,471,237); it checked both zero boundary compositions and obtained integer ranks (49,234,237), with sole nonunit Smith factor 2 for the third boundary. In the short exact sequence from homology to the cokernel of the incoming boundary and then to the image of the outgoing boundary, the last term is free; hence all cokernel torsion lies in homology. The Betti vector (1,0,0,0) then gives precisely the asserted reduced H2=Z/2. The proof does not infer simple connectivity or a homotopy type.
residual_risks: This is an independent finite computation of the stated board and action, not formal verification or a general-board theorem.

value.rationale: The board and full rigid symmetry group are canonical, not arbitrary parameters. The exact invariant distinguishes a rationally acyclic orbit space from an integrally acyclic one and shows that the symmetry quotient contributes torsion absent in the known underlying king complex. This gives a useful integral benchmark for other chessboard quotients, independently of any general classification.
residual_risks: Value is limited to an exact homology classification of this orbit space; no general theory or homotopy classification is established.
